existing_mapping.evidence: The UML diagram represents a system managing inventory, customers, and orders, which aligns with the 'Cheers' system's goals.
SaleEmployee places orders and is associated with orders as the assigned employee.
Order class contains attributes like orderNumber, orderDate, status, shipmentDate, and assigned SaleEmployee.
There is no depiction of external delivery management, reinforcing it's outside the system's scope.
RegularOrder and CustomerOrder classes show how multiple wines and quantities are tracked for customers in orders.
Customer class includes delivery information, first contact date, and personal details.
The association between Employee and Customer allows employees to order wines under customer conditions.
UrgentOrder class exists which is handled separately from RegularOrder, indicating priority in processing.
UrgentOrder class includes priorityLevel and expectedDeliveryTime attributes for priority and delivery specifics.
RegularOrder allows multiple customers in one order through its relation with CustomerOrder.
RegularOrder tracks orders by containing multiple CustomerOrder instances and a main customer.
Customer and Employee work as orderers for urgent and regular orders with recorded ID and contact details.
MarketingEmployee class contains methods to update wine and wine type information indicating permissions.
SaleEmployee has access to functions related to wine recommendation and inventory report, implying browsing capability.
WineType class has serialNumber and name attributes for identification.
WineType associates with FoodPairing, including dishName and limited recipe URLs, indicating detailed wine types.
MarketingEmployee can add and recommend DrinkingOccasion with description, season, location attributes on WineType.
MarketingEmployee imports manufacturer data via importGefenData method, associating with Wine production.
Manufacturer class maintains detailed manufacturer info, agreeing with the guideline on unique identifier storage.
Wine class captures attributes like name, description, production year, price, sweetness level, and image.
Wine is associated uniquely with its catalogNumber and manufacturer within the UML diagram.
MarketingEmployee manages Wine and WineType, including modifying price and images.
WineStorage links WineType and StorageLocation, each with unique identifiers maintained.
WineStorage tracks wine quantities at specific StorageLocations, maintaining inventory consistency.
Inventory updates are exemplified by the updateQuantity operation in WineStorage.
SaleEmployee generates various reports, including unproductive employees and inventory, aligning with report requirements.
